info.title: ZAP CRM BR — Public API
info.summary: REST API to drive a self-hosted ZAP CRM BR instance from your own scripts and automations.
info.description:
The public API lets you operate a ZAP CRM BR account from your own scripts and automations (n8n, Zapier-style integrations, cron jobs) without going through the dashboard UI — send messages, manage contacts, launch broadcast campaigns, and subscribe to outbound event webhooks.

Every request authenticates with an **API key** (`Authorization: Bearer wacrm_live_...`), created in the dashboard under **Settings → API keys** by an admin or owner. A key is scoped to exactly one account — there is no cross-account access — and only does what the [scopes](#tag/Meta) granted to it allow.

**An API key is an account-wide credential, not an agent identity.** It sees every conversation and message in the account, including threads assigned to other agents — there is no per-agent row-level isolation over the public API (that isolation exists only inside the dashboard, enforced by Postgres RLS keyed on the signed-in user). Treat a key like an administrator credential and issue one per integration so it can be revoked in isolation.

All error text on `/api/**` (including this API) is **English by design** — integrations, scripts, and logs consume a stable language; do not expect or rely on localized error payloads.

Source of truth for this contract: `docs/public-api.md` in the ZAP CRM BR repository. This `openapi.json` is generated from — and must be kept in sync with — that document.

tags.description: Inbound webhook — a third party creates a contact (and optionally launches a template) by calling ZAP CRM BR. The inverse of Webhooks, which notify third parties about ZAP CRM BR events.

get.summary: Verify a key and discover its scopes
get.description: Returns the account a key is bound to and the scopes it carries. Requires only a valid key — no scope. Use it to verify a key works before wiring up real calls; it also exercises the entire public-API auth stack end to end (bearer parse → hash lookup → liveness → rate limit → envelope).

200.description: The account and scopes this key is bound to.

post.description:
Send a WhatsApp message to a phone number. You pass an **E.164 number**, not an internal conversation id — the endpoint finds-or-creates the contact + conversation, then sends.

**`cold_send_limit` (429).** On a WhatsApp QRCode (Evolution) channel with no active 24h Meta session window, outbound-to-a-cold-contact is throttled by a per-instance daily/hourly cap and a minimum interval between cold sends (SPEC 049 §6.2). This path **always blocks** when the limit is hit — stricter than the dashboard inbox, which only warns a human agent. Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

429.description: Per-key rate limit exceeded (`rate_limited`), or the WhatsApp QRCode cold-send limit was hit (`cold_send_limit`). Both carry `Retry-After`.

error.message: Rate limit exceeded for this API key

502.description: The request reached Meta and Meta rejected the send (`meta_error`).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free-text filter, matched against contact name or phone.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Restrict to contacts carrying this tag id.

post.description: Create a contact. An existing match by phone returns `200` with the existing contact (no duplicate is created); a genuinely new contact returns `201`.

200.description: An existing contact already matched this phone number — returned as-is (no duplicate created).

patch.description: Updates only the fields present in the request body — omitted fields are left untouched. Pass `tags` (an array of tag names, created if missing) to **replace** the contact's full tag set.

get.description: List conversations, newest first. **An API key sees the whole account** — assigned and unassigned conversations alike, regardless of which agent they're assigned to.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: Restrict to conversations on this channel (SPEC 049 §5.4) — e.g. one specific WhatsApp QRCode instance.

get.description: List a conversation's messages, newest first. The conversation is verified to belong to your account before any message is returned (`404` otherwise).

post.description:
Launch a template broadcast to a list of recipients. The broadcast + its recipient rows are persisted immediately and the sends fan out in the background with a soft 60-second budget, so the call returns fast — poll `GET /broadcasts/{id}` for progress. Recipients are capped at **1000 per request**; invalid phone numbers are dropped and counted as `rejected` rather than failing the whole call.

A request near the 1000-recipient cap can exceed the fan-out's 60-second budget — there is no durable retry queue yet, so recipients still `pending` when the budget runs out stay `pending` rather than resuming automatically. Prefer splitting large sends into a few smaller requests.

202.description: The broadcast was accepted and sending has started in the background.

get.description: `status` moves `sending` → `sent`; `delivered_count` / `read_count` keep climbing as Meta delivery webhooks arrive after the initial send completes.

200.description: The broadcast's current status and counters.

post.summary: Create a contact from an inbound webhook (and optionally send a template)
post.description:
The inverse of `/webhooks`: a third party (n8n, a landing page, an e-commerce platform) POSTs here to create or match a contact, write tags/notes/custom fields, and — when `template_id` is approved — send a template. Every accepted request also feeds a funnel: a `broadcasts` row scoped by `webhook_id`, reused across every request that carries the same id (SPEC 055).

**Phone validation here is stricter than `POST /contacts`:** Brazilian DDD and mobile/landline shape are enforced — this endpoint is new, so tightening the rule breaks no existing integration.

**Failure asymmetry.** Before the contact is created, a failure is `400` — nothing was written. After the contact exists, a failure is always `202`, with the problem reported in `warnings[]` — never a 4xx/5xx, so a caller retry can never duplicate the contact (notes, in particular, are never deduplicated). A request rejected for a missing/invalid key (`401`/`403`/`429`) logs nothing — there's no account to attach a log row to.

202.description: Accepted — the contact was created or matched. The template send (if any) runs in the background and is never awaited by this response.

400.description: Rejected before the contact was created (`invalid_webhook_id`, `invalid_webhook_name`, `invalid_phone`, or `bad_request`) — nothing was written.

error.message: 'webhook_id' must be a numeric string with at least 16 digits
'webhook_name' is required and must not be empty
Phone number failed Brazilian validation: invalid_ddd

get.description: List your account's registered webhook endpoints. Never returns the signing secret.

post.description:
Register an HTTPS endpoint to receive event deliveries. **The response includes `secret` exactly once** — store it to verify the `X-Wacrm-Signature` header on deliveries; the CRM keeps only an encrypted copy and can never show it again.

The target `url` must resolve to a public address: `localhost`, private/RFC1918 ranges, link-local addresses (including the `169.254.169.254` cloud-metadata address), and similar internal targets are refused (SSRF guard).

patch.description: Update `url`, `events`, and/or `is_active` — at least one field is required. Setting `is_active: true` on a previously auto-disabled endpoint also resets its consecutive-failure counter to 0.

bearerAuth.description: An API key created in the dashboard under Settings → API keys, sent as `Authorization: Bearer wacrm_live_...`. Scopes are enforced per-endpoint; see each operation's required scope.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's `meta.next_cursor`. Pass back verbatim — never construct or parse it. A malformed/unrecognized cursor is treated as absent (restarts from the first page).

RetryAfter.description: Seconds until the caller should retry.

RateLimitLimit.description: The request budget for the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests still allowed in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the window resets.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, revoked, or expired API key (`unauthorized`). These cases are deliberately indistinguishable on the wire.

Forbidden.description: The key is valid but lacks the scope this endpoint requires (`forbidden`).

error.message: This API key is missing the 'messages:send' scope

NotFound.description: No such resource, or it belongs to another account (`not_found`). Never `403` for a cross-account id — that would confirm the id exists.

error.message: Rate limit exceeded for this API key

InternalError.description: Server error (`internal`). The message never leaks internal detail.

ApiScope.description: A key's capabilities are defined entirely by the scopes granted to it at creation.

code.description: Stable, machine-matchable error code — branch on this, not on `message`.

message.description: Human-facing text. May be reworded; do not pattern-match on it.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page.

tags.description: Tag names. Any name that doesn't yet exist is created.

ContactUpdateRequest.description: Every field is optional; only fields present in the body are changed. A field set to `null` clears it (for `name`/`email`/`company`).

tags.description: Tag names. Replaces the contact's full tag set (pass `[]` to clear all tags).

channel_id.description: Which of the account's channels this conversation belongs to (SPEC 049 §5.4). `null` only for a row that predates multi-channel support.

interactive_reply_id.description: The `id` of the interactive button/list row the contact tapped, when this message is a reply to one.

id.description: Stable id, echoed back when the recipient taps this button.

buttons.description: 1 to 3 buttons. Ids must be unique within the message.

id.description: Stable id, echoed back when the recipient selects this row.

sections.description: Up to 10 sections; 1 to 10 rows TOTAL across all sections. Row ids must be unique across the whole message.

params.description: Positional body variables as an array, or a structured `{ header, body, buttons }` object.

to.description: E.164 phone number. Find-or-creates the contact + conversation.

reply_to_message_id.description: Must be a message in the same conversation.

channel_id.description: Which of the account's channels to send from (SPEC 049 §5.4). Omit to use the account's default channel.

name.description: Name to give a newly-created contact. Ignored if the contact already exists.

contact_created.description: True if `to` didn't match an existing contact.

params.description: Positional template body variables for this recipient.

rejected.description: Recipients dropped for an invalid phone number.

is_active.description: Auto-set to `false` after 15 consecutive delivery failures. Re-enable with PATCH, which also resets the failure counter.

failure_count.description: Consecutive delivery failures. Reset to 0 by any successful delivery or by re-enabling via PATCH.

secret.description: The HMAC signing secret, in plaintext. Shown exactly once, at creation — store it now. Prefixed `whsec_`.

url.description: Must be `https://` and resolve to a public address.

WebhookUpdateRequest.description: At least one field is required.

field.description: Matched case-insensitively against an existing custom field name in this account. No match (or an ambiguous one) skips this entry — never fails the request.

webhook_id.description: Digits only, minimum 16 characters — identifies the FUNNEL this request feeds, reused across every request carrying the same id. Not a credential; the API key is.

webhook_name.description: Display label for the funnel. Non-empty after trim; truncated (not rejected) past 120 characters. The last request's value wins.

phone.description: Validated with strict Brazilian rules (DDD against the Anatel list, mobile/landline shape) — stricter than `POST /contacts`.

name.description: Falls back to the normalized phone if omitted.

tags.description: Additive — never removes a tag the contact already has. Creates a tag that doesn't exist yet.

oneOf.description: Indexed object, e.g. `{"nota_1": "…", "nota_2": "…"}`. Keys are sorted by their NUMERIC SUFFIX (`nota_2` before `nota_10`), not alphabetically.

notes.description: Always appends — never dedupes or replaces existing notes.

template_id.description: A `message_templates.id` in this account, with Meta status `APPROVED`.

template_params.description: Positional body variables (`{{1}}`, `{{2}}`…) for the template. Non-string entries are coerced to string, never dropped — dropping would shift every later placeholder.

IngestFunnelRef.description: `null` only when the funnel row itself couldn't be created/updated (a rare infra failure) — the contact is still created in that case.

contact_created.description: True if `phone` didn't match an existing contact.

linked.description: Requested tags that already existed on the account.

created.description: Requested tags that were newly created.

skipped.description: Field names that had no match (or an ambiguous one) and were skipped.

attempted.description: True when `template_id` was present and a send was queued — NOT a guarantee it succeeded; see `warnings[]` and the dashboard log for the outcome.
